coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across database visualization, graph visualization, data engineering, business intelligence, and adjacent analytics markets. Sources cover: (1) Analyst reports on data visualization market sizing (Gartner, Forrester, IDC, MarketsandMarkets, Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, Fortune Business Insights); (2) Graph database market segment (separate 24-27% CAGR, driven by cloud, AI/ML, real-time analytics); (3) Industry verticals: healthcare analytics (19-26% CAGR), BFSI BI (11-12% CAGR), manufacturing analytics (17-21% CAGR); (4) Related segments: low-code/no-code platforms (19-29% CAGR), data engineering services (13-24% CAGR), data observability (8-17% CAGR), augmented analytics (25-30% CAGR), self-service analytics (15-18% CAGR), streaming analytics (12-33% CAGR), embedded analytics (11-16% CAGR), metadata management (21-26% CAGR), CDP (19-30% CAGR), knowledge graphs (14-21% CAGR); (5) Competitive intelligence: Gartner Magic Quadrant and Forrester Wave leaders (Tableau, Power BI, ThoughtSpot, Qlik, Oracle, Google); open-source ecosystem (Metabase, Apache Superset); cloud data warehouse ecosystem (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift); (6) Funding data from Crunchbase, PitchBook, Dealroom; (7) Trends and adoption: data literacy gaps (83% of orgs), AI integration acceleration, cloud dominance (50-63% market share), semantic layers, real-time analytics, self-service democratization. Whole-market estimates: data visualization $10.92B (2025), business intelligence $35-50B (2025-2026), broader analytics ecosystem $150B+. Top-down: $10.92B data-viz × 3-5x for broader BI/analytics ecosystem = addressable market. Bottom-up: 150k+ BI/analytics tool users × $5-50k per seat = $750M-$7.5B SAM within SMB/mid-market segment. Wide geographic coverage (North America 37%, APAC 11% CAGR). Deduped across 45+ sources; avoided overlap between vendor blogs and analyst reports. Notable gaps: specific product revenue data (non-public companies), detailed pricing models for visualization-only tools, granular TAM for graph visualization specifically (subsumed under graph databases), academic citations on HCI/visualization theory (out of scope for market leaf).
